name: Augustan Dyarchy
description: Balance the princeps' household administration with senatorial commissions and equestrian execution.
note: A gameplay path for the republic-facade settlement, not two legally equal sovereign powers.

name: Provincial Principate
description: Broaden provincial petitions, civic mediation, and equestrian administration within imperial rule.
note: Abstracts greater provincial consultation without inventing representative government.

name: Memorialist Han Court
description: Give formal memorials, remonstrance, and reviewed appointments greater weight at the imperial court.
note: Models documented memorial practice without projecting later examination institutions.

name: Commandery Supervision
description: Strengthen audited commandery returns, rotating inspectors, and direct imperial appointment.
note: Represents stronger oversight while preserving local variation and court politics.

name: Great-House Compact
description: Entrust mounted service and regional judgment to leading houses under negotiated royal precedence.
note: A high-autonomy Arsacid path; exact constitutional procedure remains unrecoverable.

name: Iranian Royal Domain
description: Expand royal estates, sealed accounts, and court-appointed officers without erasing great houses.
note: Combines attested royal-domain tendencies across a broad Iranian profile.

name: Boule and Magistracies
description: Center civic administration on audited magistracies, council rotations, and public benefaction.
note: A civic constitutional path whose franchise remains locally variable.

name: Federal Synedrion
description: Coordinate member communities through shared delegates, sanctuary diplomacy, and bounded contributions.
note: Uses a conservative federal-council adapter rather than one universal league constitution.

name: Lineage Rotation
description: Rotate recognized lineage delegates and offices to preserve collective legitimacy.
note: A gameplay abstraction for oligarchic collective office, not a fixed franchise.

name: Muster Confederacy
description: Bind assembly rights to witnessed military, road, and granary contributions.
note: Connects collective defense to assembly bargaining without inventing a standing federation.

name: Wing Confederacy
description: Formalize left-right command, lineage musters, and negotiated pasture circuits.
note: Avoids projecting later decimal ranks onto first-century confederations.

name: Prestige-Gift Court
description: Concentrate envoys, tribute gifts, and brokered appointments around the ruling lineage.
note: Models gift circulation as political infrastructure, not a salaried bureaucracy.

name: Elder-Moot Kingship
description: Require leading-kindred and ritual assent for musters, settlements, and succession bargains.
note: A regional floor for varied assemblies, not a single Germanic or Celtic constitution.

name: Warband-Retinue Kingship
description: Shift authority toward gift-bound retainers and a ruler able to sustain repeated campaigns.
note: Represents retinue consolidation without assuming later feudal vassalage.

name: Temple-Endowment Court
description: Govern through protected cult endowments, scribal custody, and ritual provisioning.
note: A cross-regional sacral path whose local temple and monastic forms remain distinct.

name: Irrigation Palace
description: Tie royal legitimacy to reservoirs, canal labor, granaries, and audited distributions.
note: A gameplay adapter for court-waterwork relationships, not universal hydraulic despotism.

name: Petition Court
description: Regularize witnessed petitions, sealed replies, and arbitration among court and urban houses.
note: A conservative royal-court path for regions lacking a narrower attested constitution.

name: Frontier-Muster Monarchy
description: Organize royal authority around fortress stores, retainer service, and route protection.
note: A bounded frontier adapter rather than a claim of one transregional military monarchy.

name: Left and Right Wing Command
description: Balance the chanyu's household with eastern and western command networks, lineage musters, and pasture arbitration.
note: Models the securely reported wing structure without importing later decimal ranks or a fixed territorial bureaucracy.

name: Chanyu Gift Circuit
description: Concentrate envoys, hostages, prestige gifts, and frontier exchange around the chanyu's itinerant court.
note: Treats recorded gift and diplomatic exchange as political infrastructure, not a salaried central chancery.

name: Fortress-Lineage Kingship
description: Broker royal commands through fortress communities, leading lineages, beacon obligations, and witnessed musters.
note: Represents an early fortress and lineage polity without projecting the mature Three Kingdoms office hierarchy backward.

name: Royal Granary Court
description: Strengthen the royal household through millet stores, artisan obligations, route signals, and rotating fortress officers.
note: A bounded centralizing path grounded in subsistence and fortified settlement rather than a recovered administrative code.

name: Dual Royal Household
description: Coordinate royal households, sealed tribute, provincial brokers, and desert-route dispatches around Meroe.
note: Uses the attested prominence of royal women and rulers without claiming two equal sovereign offices in every reign.

name: Temple-Domain Stewardship
description: Entrust cult storehouses, Nile contributions, metalwork returns, and provincial hospitality to protected stewards.
note: Combines attested cult and material contexts without inventing a uniform Meroitic temple bureaucracy.

name: Reservoir Stewardship Kingship
description: Ground royal legitimacy in reservoir accounts, labor rotations, elephant service, and regional petition circuits.
note: Models securely important irrigation patronage while avoiding the claim of one centralized hydraulic administration.

name: Sangha Endowment Court
description: Balance royal patronage, monastic endowments, port measures, and regional lineages through recorded grants.
note: Represents early Buddhist patronage and donation practice without importing later monastic landholding arrangements wholesale.

name: Highland Dynast Compact
description: Entrust fortress commands, mounted service, pass security, and arbitration to leading highland houses under royal precedence.
note: Dynastic and fortress bargaining is evidence-bounded; no single written Artaxiad compact or fixed rank order is claimed.

name: Artaxata Royal-Domain Court
description: Strengthen royal domains, sealed accounts, pass couriers, and embassy coordination without erasing highland dynasts.
note: A centralizing gameplay branch grounded in royal-domain and route functions, not a recovered Artaxiad chancery.

name: Cistern Stewardship Court
description: Ground royal legitimacy in cisterns, channels, oasis labor, sanctuary stores, and predictable water compacts.
note: Water management is securely important, while this branch avoids claiming one centralized kingdom-wide hydraulic administration.

name: Caravan Customs Court
description: Empower caravan, merchant, and artisan houses through protected routes, stable measures, and reviewed customs schedules.
note: The branch represents caravan and customs leverage without reducing the Nabataean kingdom to a modern commercial state.

name: Highland Irrigation Court
description: Coordinate terrace walls, dams, water release, storage, and seasonal repair through protected cultivating communities.
note: A highland waterwork branch grounded in material context, not a claim for a uniform Himyarite hydraulic bureaucracy.

name: Incense-Route Court
description: Center royal coordination on incense assessment, protected inland routes, Red Sea dispatches, and port measures.
note: Incense and maritime exchange are securely relevant, while exact court offices and assessed shares remain unrecoverable.

name: Guild and Caravan Court
description: Regularize guild gifts, caravan passage, inspected measures, water access, and royal hospitality across Deccan routes.
note: Uses attested exchange and donation contexts without projecting later guild constitutions uniformly into AD 1.

name: Maharathi and Mahabhoja Compact
description: Entrust regional service, elephant and mounted musters, route protection, and local arbitration to titled houses.
note: Attested titles support a regional-house branch, but their precise AD 1 competence and hierarchy are not reconstructed.

name: Dynastic Mint Court
description: Center royal authority on witnessed weights, dies, prestige exchange, retinue gifts, and succession display at the oppida.
note: Coinage and dynastic display are securely relevant, while the branch avoids inventing a centralized mint bureaucracy or monetary economy.

name: Oppida Compact
description: Coordinate stores, craft measures, sanctuary hearings, cultivating households, and Channel exchange among fortified settlement centers.
note: Oppida provide a defensible settlement framework, not proof of an equal federation, fixed franchise, or uniform administration.

name: Maroboduus's Retinue Court
description: Concentrate gifts, arms, intelligence, frontier envoys, and repeated campaign service around the royal following.
note: The ruler's organized following is securely important; this path does not turn personal bonds into medieval vassalage or salaried office.

name: Allied Host Compact
description: Distribute settlement, wagon, warrior, provisioning, and frontier-watch obligations among negotiated allied kindreds.
note: The branch models negotiated host contributions without claiming a permanent federation, equal member peoples, or fixed territorial levies.

name: Ma'rib Irrigation Court
description: Ground royal legitimacy in dam masonry, canal clearing, measured releases, cultivation, and bounded seasonal labor.
note: The Ma'rib water system is secure, while the branch avoids hydraulic-despotism claims or a uniform kingdom-wide water bureaucracy.

name: Sanctuary and Incense-Route Court
description: Balance sanctuary inventories, incense assessments, caravan water, protected passage, and Red Sea forwarding.
note: Sanctuary and incense-route contexts are securely important, while exact AD 1 court competences and assessed shares remain uncertain.

name: Caesarea Urban Court
description: Strengthen civic petitions, port returns, inspected craft measures, dynastic diplomacy, and accountable royal workshops.
note: Juba's court and urban patronage support the branch without implying that every community shared a Roman civic constitution.

name: Mounted Frontier Compact
description: Entrust mounted watch, guides, water access, regional musters, and border intelligence to negotiated frontier communities.
note: Mounted frontier service is modeled conservatively without flattening diverse Mauretanian communities into a single tribal institution.

name: Jerusalem Temple Court
description: Give temple stores, priestly hearings, pilgrimage order, and sanctuary provisioning a larger place in ethnarchic government.
note: The Jerusalem temple establishment is securely central, while this branch does not treat priestly authority as a uniform civil bureaucracy.

name: Judean Toparchy Compact
description: Work through regional assessment districts, cultivating communities, cistern upkeep, market peace, and witnessed local petitions.
note: Toparchic districts and local assessment are defensible, but their precise AD 1 competences and representative character remain uncertain.

name: Cappadocian Domain Court
description: Concentrate sealed accounts, royal estates, sanctuary inventories, and appointed custodians around Archelaus's household.
note: Royal-domain and sanctuary interests are historically grounded, while the exact reach of a centralized domain administration is not reconstructed.

name: Cappadocian Pass Compact
description: Entrust caravan passage, highland watch, cavalry musters, and market safe-conducts to negotiated regional houses and towns.
note: Cappadocia's routes and mounted households support this branch without implying a recovered fixed council or uniform pass law.

name: Odrysian Dynastic Court
description: Concentrate royal seals, succession hearings, retinue gifts, city diplomacy, and Roman embassies around the ruling house.
note: Dynastic fragmentation and Roman intervention are secure contexts, but the precise AD 1 court hierarchy and Pythodoris's role remain contested.

name: Thracian Mountain Host
description: Distribute pass watch, horse service, timber and grain provisioning, sanctuary oaths, and frontier warning among regional communities.
note: The branch models negotiated regional service without flattening Thracian peoples into a single tribe or inventing a permanent federal host.

name: Bosporan Polis Court
description: Give grain measures, harbor petitions, sanctuary inventories, and civic mediation greater weight in royal government.
note: Greek poleis and grain ports securely structured Bosporan power, while their local constitutions and leverage varied.

name: Bosporan Steppe Compact
description: Broker mounted service, pasture access, frontier intelligence, claimant support, and strait defense with regional households.
note: Mounted and steppe-frontier interests are defensible, but this path avoids inventing one ethnic bloc, fixed treaty, or recovered council.

name: Galilean Lake Court
description: Center tetrarchic administration on fisheries, landing places, market measures, storage, and road peace around the lake settlements.
note: Fisheries and market exchange are defensible functions, while one centralized lake administration or royal monopoly is not claimed.

name: Galilean-Peraean Compact
description: Work through regional houses, pastoral communities, water access, road service, and witnessed local assessment across the divided tetrarchy.
note: The geographical division and route obligations are secure contexts, but no representative compact or uniform Peraean institution is reconstructed.

name: Batanean Highland Court
description: Concentrate sealed grants, basalt settlement works, cistern returns, sanctuary inventories, and appointed route custodians around Philip's household.
note: Settlement, water, and sanctuary functions are grounded, while their concentration in a uniform tetrarchic administration remains a gameplay path.

name: Batanean Frontier Compact
description: Entrust highland watch, guides, horse service, pasture and water access, and restitution to negotiated northern communities.
note: The branch models highland and frontier service without inventing one Batanean ethnic bloc, fixed treaty, or permanent host.

name: Commagenean Sanctuary Court
description: Give sanctuary inventories, dynastic display, hospitality, orchard gifts, and ritual custody greater weight in royal government.
note: Commagene's dynastic-sanctuary setting is secure, while this branch does not reconstruct a kingdom-wide priestly bureaucracy.

name: Euphrates Passage Compact
description: Entrust ferry safety, stable weights, caravan passage, landing stores, and compensation to negotiated river and merchant houses.
note: Euphrates passage and exchange are secure contexts, but no complete Commagenean ferry code or merchant council is recovered.

name: Emesan Sanctuary Court
description: Center dynastic legitimacy on sanctuary stores, ritual hospitality, offerings, lamps, textiles, and protected custodianship.
note: Emesa's sanctuary importance is defensible, while exact AD 1 priestly offices and their relationship to Iamblichus II remain unrecoverable.

name: Orontes Caravan Compact
description: Entrust route security, pack service, textile measures, water, escorts, and compensation to caravan and city houses.
note: Caravan and urban exchange support the branch without implying a surviving uniform customs code or permanent merchant constitution.
